title: 2021 Sydney Tech Legal Studies Trial
notes: No answer key was included in the PDF. all answers are reasoned guesses.

questions.stem:
Julie, an unemployed single mother, bashes a 90 year old lady and steals her wallet.

What is an aggravating factor in sentencing Julie?
questions.answerNote: The victim’s advanced age is an aggravating circumstance.

questions.stem:
Harry is charged with murder.

What court has original jurisdiction in hearing this case?
questions.answerNote: Murder is an indictable offence heard at first instance in the Supreme Court.

questions.stem: Under what process can South Australia Police return Kevin to NSW to face charges of extortion?
questions.answerNote: Interstate extradition returns an accused person to the state where the charge is to be heard.

questions.stem: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is an example of which of the following?
questions.answerNote: The Declaration is not a treaty; Many of its principles are recognised as customary international law.

questions.stem:
Bailey was convicted of having child pornography on his electronic devices. After being sentenced to 5 years imprisonment he was placed in isolation.

What is this an example of?
questions.answerNote: Placement in isolation after sentence is a decision made during the administration of the sentence.

questions.stem:
Some Australian businesses have been underpaying their workers.

What is this a breach of?

options.A: The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
options.B: The International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights

questions.answerNote: Fair remuneration and just working conditions are protected under the ICESCR.

questions.stem: When sentencing a child convicted of a criminal offence, what guidelines do magistrates follow?

options.A: Deterrence is more important than restitution
options.B: A fine should be imposed whenever possible
options.C: A child’s education must never be disrupted
options.D: A custodial sentence as a last resort

questions.answerNote: Youth justice principles treat detention as a last resort.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of circle sentencing?

options.B: Reduce recidivism in Aboriginal and Torres Strait communities

questions.answerNote: Circle sentencing is aimed at reducing reoffending in Aboriginal communities (B); Rehabilitation (A) is a weaker second option.

questions.stem:
Peter is charged with murder after he hit his partner over the head with a frying pan. In the past, Peter’s partner had assaulted him on numerous occasions. During his trial, Peter successfully raised a defence and was found guilty of manslaughter.

Which defence did he raise?
questions.answerNote: Provocation can reduce a murder conviction to manslaughter; Self-defence would result in acquittal if successful.

questions.stem: Which organisation has the power to prosecute ISIS for the execution of civilians in Jordan?
questions.answerNote: The ICC prosecutes individuals for international crimes, subject to its jurisdiction.

questions.stem: What is the role of the jury in a criminal trial?

options.A: Ask questions of the alleged offender
options.B: Make suggestions about a suitable punishment
options.C: Decide the innocence of the alleged offender
options.D: Decide the guilt of the alleged offender

questions.answerNote: The jury determines guilt; Sentencing is for the judge.

questions.stem: The role of the UN General Assembly is to hear which of the following cases?

options.B: Human right issues brought by individuals
options.D: Challenges to the rule of law by nation states

questions.answerNote: Unsure: the General Assembly debates and recommends on rule-of-law challenges by states (D); Disputes between states (C) are decided by the ICJ.

questions.stem:
Jimmy hacks into the university computer and changes the results of his final year exams.

What type of crime did Jimmy commit?
questions.answerNote: Computer hacking to alter records is an economic or property related offence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an argument in favour of Australia having a Charter of Rights?

options.A: It would give the United Nations more say in Australian legislation
options.B: It would give better legal protection to vulnerable members of our society
options.C: It would balance the community’s rights with their responsibilities
options.D: It would decrease the power of common law in the legal response to social issues

questions.answerNote: A Charter can provide clearer domestic protection for people whose rights are vulnerable.

questions.stem: What is universal suffrage?

options.A: Right not to be exploited by sovereign states
options.B: Right to live in a healthy environment
options.C: Right to vote in government elections
options.D: Right to a basic level of education

questions.answerNote: Universal suffrage is the right of eligible citizens to vote.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a transnational crime?
questions.answerNote: People trafficking is the standard transnational crime example. Selling sex slaves (A) could also be transnational, but D is the clearer fit.

questions.stem:
Transport NSW installs CCTV on both manned and unmanned train platforms.

What is this an example of?
questions.answerNote: CCTV increases surveillance and changes the opportunity for crime, which is situational prevention.

questions.stem:
A NSW police officer does not issue a fine to two teenagers breaching the NSW COVID-19 stay at home laws.

What is this an example of?
questions.answerNote: An officer choosing whether to take enforcement action is exercising discretion.

questions.stem: Charles was arrested in Sydney and charged with human trafficking. In which court would this case be heard?
questions.answerNote: Human trafficking is a Commonwealth offence tried in the state courts; The Supreme Court of NSW is the only plausible listed domestic court.

questions.stem: The police suspect Samantha of carrying a carving knife which was used in an attack. What powers of search and seizure do the police have?

options.A: Search Samantha and confiscate the knife if they have a warrant
options.B: Only search Samantha and confiscate the knife if they arrest her
options.C: Confiscate the knife but not search Samantha without arresting her
options.D: Search Samantha without a warrant and confiscate the knife

questions.answerNote: NSW police may search a person without a warrant where statutory reasonable-suspicion grounds apply and seize evidence found.
